advances:
Gives a joint trace-interval compatibility condition for one
\(A_0\)-polygon with exact support
\[
P_j,P_0,P_\ell,P_{k\ell}.
\]
The vertical \(p_j=0\) trace and diagonal \(p_k=0\) trace force, by
perspective through their convex hull, a subinterval of the horizontal
\(p_\ell=0\) trace.  Convex hulls of adjacent trace intervals also
charge explicit area to \(P_0\) and \(P_\ell\).  These constraints retain
the three interval offsets discarded by separate sharp-chord bounds.
The new strict-trace scalar calibration admits exact rational offsets
satisfying every derived condition with slack, so this lemma does not
exclude it.  The remaining \(A_0\)-layer is exact convex boundary
completion with the four prescribed cell areas.
author: mp_r90_opposite_support_gap_full_hypotheses
proof:
We first locate the three full sections.  The strict supported chambers
in the coordinates (1) are
\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
P_j&X<0,\ Y>0,\ X+Y<\delta,\\
P_0&X>0,\ Y>0,\ X+Y<\delta,\\
P_\ell&X>0,\ Y<0,\ X+Y<\delta,\\
P_{k\ell}&X>0,\ Y<0,\ X+Y>\delta.
\end{array}
\tag{19}
\]
Every positive-area cell contains an interior point of \(A\) with its
strict sign pattern.

If a point of \(A\cap\{X=0\}\) had \(Y<0\), moving it slightly toward
an interior point of \(P_j\) would enter the unsupported strict chamber
\(P_{j\ell}\).  If it had \(Y>\delta\), moving it slightly toward an
interior point of \(P_0\) would enter the unsupported strict chamber
\(P_k\).  Hence this whole section lies on
\[
X=0,\qquad0\le Y\le\delta.
\]
Positive area in \(P_j,P_0\) puts interior points on both sides of
\(X=0\), so the line meets \(\operatorname{int}A\) and its section is
a nondegenerate interval under (3).

If a point of \(A\cap\{Y=0\}\) had \(X<0\), moving it slightly toward
an interior point of \(P_\ell\) would enter \(P_{j\ell}\).  If it had
\(X>\delta\), moving it slightly toward an interior point of \(P_0\)
would enter \(P_k\).  Thus this section lies on
\[
Y=0,\qquad0\le X\le\delta.
\]
The positive cells \(P_0,P_\ell\) put the line through
\(\operatorname{int}A\).

Finally, on \(X+Y=\delta\), a point with \(Y>0,X>0\) can be moved
slightly toward an interior point of \(P_{k\ell}\) to enter the
unsupported chamber \(P_k\).  If instead \(Y>0,X\le0\), the same
motion enters \(P_{jk}\) when \(X<0\), and enters \(P_k\) when
\(X=0\).  Hence
\[
X+Y=\delta,\qquad Y\le0,\qquad X\ge\delta.
\]
The positive cells \(P_\ell,P_{k\ell}\) lie on opposite sides of this
line, so its section also meets \(\operatorname{int}A\).

These observations prove the representations (5)-(6).  The relative
interior of each chord lies in \(\operatorname{int}A\), and a small
ball there meets both supported adjacent chambers.  Taking closures
includes endpoints and cutting-line vertices.  Coordinate arclength on
the three lines gives the trace identities (7).

We next prove the perspective condition.  For
\[
(0,y)\in A\cap\{X=0\},\qquad
(\delta+t,-t)\in A\cap\{X+Y=\delta\},
\]
the segment joining them lies in \(A\).  If \(y+t>0\), its intersection
with \(Y=0\) has first coordinate
\[
\frac{y(\delta+t)}{y+t}=F(y,t).
\tag{20}
\]
On \(0\le y\le\delta\), \(t\ge0\),
\[
\frac{\partial F}{\partial y}
=\frac{t(\delta+t)}{(y+t)^2}\ge0,
\qquad
\frac{\partial F}{\partial t}
=\frac{y(y-\delta)}{(y+t)^2}\le0.
\tag{21}
\]
Therefore all such intersections fill an interval whose extreme
coordinates are
\[
F(\alpha,\gamma+K),
\qquad
F(\alpha+J,\gamma).
\]
The full \(Y=0\) section of \(A\) is (5l), so it must contain this
interval.  This proves (9)-(10).  The conventions (14)-(15) follow
directly by taking the indicated endpoint segments; no division by zero
is used.

For the first area charge, the convex hull of the vertical and
horizontal intervals in (5j),(5l) lies in \(A\).  It also lies in the
closed central chamber
\[
X\ge0,\qquad Y\ge0,\qquad X+Y\le\delta.
\]
Its coordinate area is
\[
\frac12\left(
(\beta+L)(\alpha+J)-\beta\alpha
\right)
=\frac12(\beta J+\alpha L+JL).
\tag{22}
\]
The coordinate area of \(\overline{P_0}\) is \(\Delta b\), proving
(11).

For the second charge, use coordinates
\[
R=-Y,\qquad T=p_k=\delta-X-Y.
\]
Their Jacobian relative to \((X,Y)\) has magnitude \(1\).  The
horizontal trace (5l) becomes the \(R=0\) interval
\[
T\in[\delta-\beta-L,\delta-\beta],
\]
while the diagonal trace (5k) becomes the \(T=0\) interval
\[
R\in[\gamma,\gamma+K].
\]
Their convex hull lies in the closed \(P_\ell\)-chamber and has
coordinate area
\[
\frac12\left(
\gamma L+(\delta-\beta-L)K+KL
\right)
=\frac12\left(\gamma L+K(\delta-\beta)\right).
\tag{23}
\]
The coordinate area of \(\overline{P_\ell}\) is \(\Delta c\), proving
(12a).

There is also a direct hull charge between the vertical and diagonal
traces.  In coordinates
\[
U=X,\qquad T=p_k=\delta-X-Y,
\]
the vertical trace becomes the \(U=0\) interval
\[
T\in[\delta-\alpha-J,\delta-\alpha],
\]
and the diagonal trace becomes the \(T=0\) interval
\[
U\in[\delta+\gamma,\delta+\gamma+K].
\]
Their convex hull lies in
\[
A\cap\{p_j\ge0,\ p_k\ge0\}
=\overline{P_0}\cup\overline{P_\ell}
\]
up to cutting-line boundaries.  Its coordinate area is
\[
\frac12\left(
(\delta+\gamma)J+(\delta-\alpha-J)K+JK
\right)
=\frac12\left(
(\delta+\gamma)J+K(\delta-\alpha)
\right).
\]
The containing union has coordinate area \(\Delta(b+c)\), proving
(12b).

For completeness, (13j)-(13l) follow from the same one-direction
concavity calculation.  In direction \(i\), let \(U\) be the coordinate
area below the cutting line, \(B=\Delta b\), and let \(\lambda\) be the
coordinate trace.  Since \(P_0\) lies in the strip of coordinate width
\(\delta\), a right supergradient of the chord profile gives
\[
U(B-\lambda\delta)_+\le\frac{\lambda^2\delta^2}{4}.
\]
The below-line physical areas are respectively
\[
a,\qquad d,\qquad c+d
\]
in the \(j,k,\ell\) directions.  Substitution gives (13j)-(13l),
including zero traces and support contacts.

It remains to test (16)-(18).  The perspective endpoints are
\[
F\left(80,\frac{201}{10}\right)
=\frac{96080}{1001},
\]
\[
F\left(\frac{801}{10},20\right)
=\frac{96120}{1001}.
\tag{24}
\]
Exact cross multiplication gives
\[
\frac{959}{10}
\le\frac{96080}{1001}
\le\frac{96120}{1001}
\le\frac{961}{10},
\]
which is (9) because
\[
\left[\beta,\beta+L\right]
=\left[\frac{959}{10},\frac{961}{10}\right].
\]
The two hull charges are
\[
\beta J+\alpha L+JL
=\frac{2561}{100}<59=2\Delta b,
\]
\[
\gamma L+K(\delta-\beta)
=\frac{441}{100}<6=2\Delta c.
\tag{25}
\]
The remaining pairwise hull charge is
\[
(\delta+\gamma)J+K(\delta-\alpha)
=14<65=2\Delta(b+c).
\tag{26}
\]
Finally, the three separate chord inequalities have left and right
sides
\[
\Delta a(\Delta b-J\delta)=\frac{39}{2}<25
=\frac{J^2\delta^2}{4},
\]
\[
\Delta d(\Delta b-K\delta)=\frac{39}{2}<25
=\frac{K^2\delta^2}{4},
\]
\[
\Delta(c+d)(\Delta b-L\delta)=38<100
=\frac{L^2\delta^2}{4}.
\tag{27}
\]
Thus the proposed rational data pass the new interval compatibility
test with strict slack.  What remains is to complete the three trace
segments to one convex polygon while adding exactly
\[
a=1,\quad b=\frac{59}{2},\quad c=3,\quad d=1
\]
in the four consecutive chambers without enlarging any trace interval.
The relations proved here are necessary for that completion but do not
claim sufficiency.  This completes the proof.
statement:
Let \(A\subset\mathbb R^2\) be a two-dimensional compact convex polygon.
Use affine coordinates
\[
p_j=X,\qquad p_\ell=Y,\qquad
p_k=\delta-X-Y,
\qquad \delta>0,
\tag{1}
\]
whose coordinate-area Jacobian is \(\Delta>0\).  Define exact cells by
\[
P_I=A\cap
\{p_i\le0\ (i\in I),\ p_i>0\ (i\notin I)\}.
\tag{2}
\]
Assume that the only positive-area cells are
\[
P_j,\qquad P_0,\qquad P_\ell,\qquad P_{k\ell},
\tag{3}
\]
with physical areas
\[
|P_j|=a,\qquad |P_0|=b,\qquad
|P_\ell|=c,\qquad |P_{k\ell}|=d.
\tag{4}
\]

The three full cutting-line sections have the forms
\[
A\cap\{X=0\}
=\{(0,y):\alpha\le y\le\alpha+J\},
\tag{5j}
\]
\[
A\cap\{Y=0\}
=\{(x,0):\beta\le x\le\beta+L\},
\tag{5l}
\]
\[
A\cap\{X+Y=\delta\}
=\{(\delta+t,-t):\gamma\le t\le\gamma+K\},
\tag{5k}
\]
where
\[
0\le\alpha\le\alpha+J\le\delta,
\qquad
0\le\beta\le\beta+L\le\delta,
\qquad
\gamma\ge0,
\tag{6}
\]
and \(J,L,K\ge0\).  In the positive-support setting (3),
\(J,L,K>0\).  They are exactly the coordinate one-sided chord traces
\[
J=\lambda_{0j},\qquad
L=\lambda_{0\ell},\qquad
K=\lambda_{0k}.
\tag{7}
\]

For \(y,t\ge0\), \(y+t>0\), put
\[
F(y,t)=\frac{y(\delta+t)}{y+t}.
\tag{8}
\]
Then the three intervals necessarily satisfy the perspective
containment
\[
\beta\le F(\alpha,\gamma+K),
\qquad
F(\alpha+J,\gamma)\le\beta+L.
\tag{9}
\]
Equivalently,
\[
\left[
F(\alpha,\gamma+K),
F(\alpha+J,\gamma)
\right]
\subseteq[\beta,\beta+L].
\tag{10}
\]
The adjacent interval hulls give the area charges
\[
\beta J+\alpha L+JL\le2\Delta b,
\tag{11}
\]
\[
\gamma L+K(\delta-\beta)\le2\Delta c.
\tag{12a}
\]
\[
(\delta+\gamma)J+K(\delta-\alpha)
\le2\Delta(b+c).
\tag{12b}
\]
Together with the three separate chord-concavity inequalities, the
complete necessary package is
\[
\Delta a(\Delta b-J\delta)_+
\le\frac{J^2\delta^2}{4},
\tag{13j}
\]
\[
\Delta d(\Delta b-K\delta)_+
\le\frac{K^2\delta^2}{4},
\tag{13k}
\]
\[
\Delta(c+d)(\Delta b-L\delta)_+
\le\frac{L^2\delta^2}{4},
\tag{13l}
\]
and (6), (9), (11), (12a), (12b).  Relations (9), (11), (12a), and
(12b) are the joint interval information absent from (13j)-(13l).

The boundary conventions are literal.  A zero-length section is a
singleton and the hull-area formulas remain valid.  In (8)-(10), use
\[
F(0,t)=0\quad(t>0),\qquad
F(y,0)=\delta\quad(y>0).
\tag{14}
\]
If the two relevant trace segments contain both \((0,0)\) and
\((\delta,0)\), their convex hull contains the entire horizontal
segment between them, so necessarily
\[
\beta=0,\qquad L=\delta.
\tag{15}
\]
This is the \(F(0,0)\) boundary case.  Vertices on one or two cutting
lines affect no cell area and are included through the closed sections
in (5).

The strict-trace scalar data
\[
(a,b,c,d)=\left(1,\frac{59}{2},3,1\right),
\qquad
\delta=100,\qquad\Delta=1,
\tag{16}
\]
\[
J=K=\frac1{10},\qquad L=\frac15
\tag{17}
\]
pass every condition above.  Exact compatible offsets for this
necessary system are
\[
\alpha=80,\qquad
\beta=\frac{959}{10},\qquad
\gamma=20.
\tag{18}
\]
This verifies only the trace-interval and area inequalities.  It is not
an assertion that a polygon with all four exact areas in (16) exists.
